title: Hosted API cost decision signal notebook
summary: Working notebook tying per-token COGS tables to operational routing signals and quick decision heuristics for Hosted API. Focus: simple triggers teams can use without running full sims. Includes light sample calculations, assumptions, and an action checklist.
body:
Status: DRAFT - notes + quick spreadsheet snippets.

Purpose:
- Capture quick, actionable heuristics mapping per-token COGS and margin thresholds -> routing/quantization/fallback actions for Hosted API customers.
- Designed to be a companion to the larger cost models (link above) but lean for on-call / PMs to make decisions.

High-level premise (short):
- We cannot run full Monte Carlos for every incident. Instead: surface 3 signals and 4 thresholds that map to deterministic actions.
- Signals are cheap to compute from existing metrics: 24h avg PPK, 95p latency by model-region, cache hit rate.

Quick signals & thresholds (candidate):
1) 24h PPK (per-1000 tokens price we pay, amortized):
   - Low: < $0.005 -> no intervention
   - Medium: $0.005 - $0.015 -> recommend cache warmup / prefer smaller model variant for non-critical routes
   - High: > $0.015 -> consider forced quantized variant / burst to lower-cost region or apply rate limiter for non-paid tier

2) 95p tail latency (client-observed) per route:
   - SLO-ok: < 250ms -> keep routing as-is
   - Degraded: 250ms - 500ms -> prefer local-region fallback variant with higher throughput
   - Severe: > 500ms -> automatic fallback to smaller model family + priority customers only

3) Cache effectiveness (prefix kv & short-term response reuse):
   - Hit rate > 40%: treat requests as batchable; increase batching window by 10%
   - Hit rate < 15%: disable aggressive batching; favor latency-optimized kernels

Operational action matrix (map combined signals -> action):
- Medium PPK + Degraded latency -> route best-effort traffic to cheaper region (if legal/region allowed) and enable 8-bit quantized variant for background endpoints.
- High PPK + Severe latency -> suspend non-production routes, spin up dedicated burst capacity (if reserved capacity available), enable conservative token limits per-request.
- Low PPK + any latency issue -> focus on infra (kernels, autoscaling) not model changes.

Sample COGS sketch (text table for quick eyeballing):
- Assumptions (global): GPU amortization share per 1k tokens = $0.006 (baseline medium-length workloads), infra overhead (orchestration, storage, egress) = $0.0015 / 1k tokens, license/third-party = $0.0008 / 1k tokens, support/ops = $0.0007 / 1k tokens.
- Derived per-model-region examples (rounded):
   - M-Family-xs (quantized q4o) in us-west: GPU+infra = $0.004 /1k, total COGS = $0.007 /1k
   - M-Family-l (unquantized fp16) in eu-west: GPU+infra = $0.011 /1k, total COGS = $0.014 /1k
   - L-Family-70b (q8) in us-east: GPU+infra = $0.020 /1k, total COGS = $0.023 /1k

Example per-request math (illustrative):
- Request: prompt 60 tokens, completion 440 tokens => 500 tokens total = 0.5k tokens
- If routed to M-Family-xs (COGS 0.007 /1k): request COGS = 0.5 * 0.007 = $0.0035
- If routed to L-Family-70b (COGS 0.023 /1k): request COGS = 0.5 * 0.023 = $0.0115
- Difference per-request ~ $0.008 -> at 1M requests/month this is ~$8k monthly delta.

Routing decision heuristics (operational checklist):
- If projected next-rolling-hour PPK exceeds tier threshold, trigger a routing policy change via Console rollout (canary 5% -> 20% over 30m).
- For non-PII workloads, prefer cross-region spillover before enabling quantized fallbacks.
- For customer SLAs with committed spend, auto-prioritize low-latency region and absorb COGS delta but flag finance.

Small spreadsheet snapshot (pasteable plain text rows):
Row headers: model_family, region, quant_mode, cogs_per_1k, typical_resp_len, notes
- M-xs, us-west, q4o, 0.007, 320, good for short chat & batchable
- M-l, eu-west, fp16, 0.014, 600, higher cost on long completion
- L-70b, us-east, q8, 0.023, 1200, high cost, high-quality

Operational playbook snippets (practical runbook):
- On-Call signal: 24h PPK > 0.015 OR 95p latency > 500ms -> Pager to infra + notify product-optimize.
- Immediate action: create Console rollout (small canary) to route non-critical tokens to M-xs in same/border region.
- Follow-up (24h): run per-route PnL extraction, tag customer segments > $X weekly, present recommended reserved capacity ask to finance.

Open questions / TODOs:
- What is the legal boundary for cross-region spillover for EMEA customers? (ask legal) @Evelyn
- Need a light-weight dashboard metric: 1h rolling PPK per-route; build as simple PromQL rule (OPT-412).
- Validate real GPU-amortization inputs: infra/ops allocations differ by cluster tag. Work with infra finance (David).
- Run an experiment: 2-week canary for opt-in customers to prefer quantized variants and measure delta in call quality and swing in PPK.

Action owners (quick):
- Marco Li: implement PromQL suggestion + add rollout template to Console (due 2025-02-26)
- Aisha Patel: draft customer communication for opt-in quantization experiment (due 2025-02-18)
- David Morales: provide updated GPU amortization numbers by region (due 2025-02-14)

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc intentionally compact; link out to long-run spreadsheets for the heavy sims.
- Avoid overfitting thresholds to a single model family; thresholds should generalize across family PPK distributions.

References / related artifacts:
- heavy model sims (internal): hosted-api-unit-econ-deep-sims (Confluence link in linked_artifacts).
- rollout automation PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-templates#87

Last edits: 2025-02-12 - consolidated heuristics after infra sync.

If this doc looks good as a lightweight playbook we should convert to 1-pager and add to Console quick-actions.
